arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Richard Dietz represented the side that brought the case. He stated Abramski filled out all required federal paperwork. He noted Abramski passed the background check. Dietz argued the statute has two possible interpretations. He emphasized this is a criminal statute.
The government argued the law targets the actual acquirer. They contended the straw purchaser is not the true buyer. They highlighted the requirement to record the final recipient's details.
Justices questioned the practical application of the law. They asked why Congress focused on the straw purchaser. They probed the distinction between the legal buyer and the final user.

paragraphs: The case tests the scope of federal firearm transfer rules. The dispute centers on whether a buyer who passes a background check but intends to give the gun to someone else commits a crime.
